blocks.text: AI Security now integrates with ServiceNow, enabling security, IT, and risk teams to sync AI Security-discovered assets and issues into existing governance and risk workflows. AI Security pushes discovered AI assets such as models, agents, MCP servers, data stores, workloads, software libraries, guardrails, code repositories, and identities into ServiceNow via Import Sets (staging tables). Your ServiceNow administrators control how staged data maps to production classes using Transform Maps.
As a part of this feature, the following changes are available in AI Security Admin Portal:

blocks.item: One-way data push from AI Security to ServiceNow for all supported AI resource types and associated security issues.
Scheduled synchronization to keep ServiceNow current with AI Security discoveries.
Security issues surfaced as incidents, problems, or custom table records in ServiceNow, linked to the corresponding AI CIs.
Flexible issue export: Create a Ticket or push to an Import Set table.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Integrating AI Security With ServiceNow.

blocks.text: The Zscaler AI Security Platform provides outbound REST APIs for AI asset management, enabling external systems such as SIEMs, SOARs, ITSM platforms, and partner integrations to programmatically access AI asset inventory and governance data.
A self-service API documentation portal provides an OpenAPI 3.1 (Swagger) interface with code samples, allowing new API consumers to authenticate and make their first API call independently.
To learn more, see Understanding Zscaler AI Security API and AI Security API.

blocks.heading: Azure Container Registry Support for AI Asset Discovery

blocks.text: AI Security can now automatically discover and catalog Azure Container Registry (ACR) repositories and their container images. This enables security administrators to gain centralized visibility into AI models, packages, and frameworks embedded in container images across their entire Azure container infrastructure.
To learn more, see Configuring Scan Rule for Azure Container Registry (ACR) Repositories, Managing Services, and IAM Roles and Permissions for Azure.

AI Security Admin Portal now supports cross-console navigation, enabling you to navigate directly from the AI Security console to the corresponding resource in your cloud service provider (CSP) console.
As part of this enhancement, changes are made to the following pages:

blocks.item: AI Infrastructure > AI Assets > MCP Servers
AI Infrastructure > AI Assets > Agents
AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Data Stores (S3 bucket, GCP storage, RDS instances, etc.)
AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Workloads (virtual machine, EC2 instance, etc.)
AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Guardrails
AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities

blocks.text: See image.

Administrators can now switch between cloud environments directly within the AI Security Admin Portal. Previously, administrators could only view data for the cloud assigned to them via Authentication Service, with no option to toggle between clouds. With this update, administrators can seamlessly switch between clouds and view data across all cloud environments from a single interface.
See image.

Zscaler AI Security introduces a new System Logs page under Administration > System Logs, with an AI Infra Scanning tab that gives administrators a unified, filterable view of every AI infrastructure scan event generated across their AWS, Azure, and GCP environments. The page displays scan outcomes including successes, failures, and detailed error messages, so administrators can quickly triage scan health, identify misconfigurations, and audit the inventory pipeline over time.
See image.
To learn more, see About System Logs - AI Infra Scanning and Downloading Reports.

blocks.heading: Enhanced Identity Inventory: Grouping, Multi-Target Visibility, and Identity Categorization

blocks.text: Zscaler AI Security introduces significant improvements to how identities are represented, visualized, and categorized on the AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities page. These enhancements give security teams clearer visibility into cross-cloud identity access and the role each identity plays in the AI ecosystem.
The following enhancements are available in the AI Security Admin Portal:

blocks.item: New filters and columns on the AI Infrastructure > AI Resources > Identities page:
Access Category: Categorizes identities based on their access type and AI usage.
Target Environment: Displays the environments that the identity can access.
Source Environment: Displays the environments from which the identity originates.
See image.
Updated General Information panel:
The Access Category and Target Environment details are now included in the identity's General Information page.
See image.

blocks.heading: AI Assets - Code Repositories: GitHub Integration

blocks.text: Zscaler AI Security Admin Portal introduces GitHub integration for AI Assets - Code Repositories, enabling administrators to automatically discover, inventory, and scan GitHub repositories for AI models, packages, frameworks, and agentic workflows embedded in source code.
As a part of this feature, the following changes are available in the AI Security Admin Portal:

blocks.item: GitHub repository onboarding: You can connect GitHub to AI Security from Administration > Account Onboarding by selecting Code Repository as the resource type and GitHub as the provider. The onboarding flow uses a GitHub OAuth App to authorize access to selected repositories.

Automated repository discovery: After authorization, AI Security automatically initiates repository discovery in the background. All discovered repositories are mapped to the Default Business Unit by default and can be reassigned post-discovery.
Granular scan rule configuration: Configure scan rules to control which repositories are scanned.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Onboarding GitHub Tenant and Configuring Scan Rule for GitHub.

blocks.heading: Embedded AI Apps Visibility in AI Asset Management

blocks.text: Zscaler AI Security Admin Portal expands the AI Asset Management platform to automatically discover and identify Embedded AI applications accessed across your organization. Security and IT teams can now gain visibility into AI-powered features within popular SaaS applications alongside traditional standalone GenAI applications.

This enhancement gives security and IT teams a complete view of their organization's AI footprint, including AI capabilities embedded within everyday SaaS applications. Teams can now strengthen AI governance by monitoring both GenAI and Embedded AI applications from a single platform, while identifying emerging AI adoption trends and shadow AI usage across departments.
See image.
To learn more, see About Public AI Inventory - Embedded AI.
The following enhancements are available in the AI Security platform.
The following widgets are added to the Public AI Overview page:

blocks.item: Upload Volume: Displays the total volume of data uploaded to public AI applications.
Download Volume: Displays the total volume of data downloaded from public AI applications.
Embedded AI Apps: Displays the number of embedded AI applications detected across your environment.

blocks.text: The following widgets are removed from the Public AI Overview page:

blocks.item: Sensitive Data
Sensitive Data Transactions

blocks.text: A new Locations tab is introduced on the Usage Insights page, enabling administrators to view AI usage insights and drill-downs based on locations.
To learn more, see About Public AI Overview and About Usage Insights.

blocks.heading: Activity-Based Detection for AWS Bedrock Model Inventory

blocks.text: The AI Security Asset Management platform now utilizes activity-based detection to precisely identify managed and custom AWS Bedrock models currently utilized by your organization. By analyzing AWS CloudTrail events, the inventory only includes models accessed within the preceding 90 days, ensuring data hygiene and accuracy.
Security teams can now access two granular perspectives for each identified model on the AI Security - Models page (AI Infrastructure > AI Assets - Models):

blocks.item: Usage Timeline: Provides visibility into the 10 most recent invocations, detailing activity trends and specific timestamps.
Top 10 Users: Lists the primary unique identities, including user names and IAM roles, along with invocation counts and last seen data.

blocks.text: To learn more, see About AI Assets - Models.

blocks.heading: Microsoft Copilot Studio Support in AI Security

blocks.text: Zscaler AI Security now supports Microsoft Copilot Studio, enabling organizations to automatically discover and secure AI agents built on the platform. This integration helps security teams proactively identify and remediate misconfigurations that could expose sensitive data across agentic AI workflows.
With this release, AI Security introduces the following capabilities:

blocks.item: Automated Agent Discovery: Automatically discovers and maintains a unified inventory of agents deployed across Copilot Studio environments, along with their associated MCP servers and knowledge bases.
Security Posture Assessment: Identifies and evaluates the security risks associated with Copilot Studio agents.
Entitlement Visibility: Provides clear visibility into who has access to each Copilot Studio agent.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Onboarding Microsoft Copilot Studio Tenant.
